title: Still smell like the shop
label: STILL SMELL LIKE THE SHOP
lead: Hook 1 (Instant recognition), because one exact, slightly funny detail, the new-shoe smell, makes the viewer feel caught in the first second.

hooks.label: STILL SMELL LIKE THE SHOP
hooks.say: Your running shoes still smell like the shop.

hooks.label: THEY GOT THE BEST SPOT
hooks.say: Your running shoes got tissue paper and the best spot by the door. Never a run.

hooks.label: WHY THEY NEVER LEAVE THE BOX
hooks.say: Why do the shoes we buy for running never leave the box?

beats.say: Your running shoes still smell like the *shop*.
beats.scene: A shoebox lid pops up and slides off. Clean white running shoes sit in tissue paper.

beats.say: You bought them on a Sunday night, and in your head, you'd already *run*.
beats.scene: The pair placed neatly by a door at night, a wall clock past eleven, laces perfect.

beats.say: Then Monday was too cold, Tuesday was too busy, and the box went under the *bed*.
beats.scene: Low angle: the shoebox slides across the floor and disappears under a bed into the dark.

beats.say: But the shoes were never the hard part. The *door* was.
beats.scene: A closed front door, a thin line of morning light under it. The camera pushes in slowly.

beats.say: So tomorrow, put them on, and walk to the end of the *street*.
beats.scene: The door swings open, warm morning light floods the floor and reaches the shoes.

beats.say: Send this to the friend whose shoes are still *white*.
beats.scene: Close on the spotless shoes in the doorway light, one lace slowly coming loose, ready.
